chunks: And Sh. Sami said in Kamus al-A'lam — Turkish — p. 668, the translation of which is:

(Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Baghdadi is among the most celebrated scholars; his honorific title is al-Shaykh al-Mufid. He enjoyed standing and esteem among the Buyid dynasty; 'Adud al-Dawla used to visit him in his home. He has numerous works; he is an ascetic, a devout worshipper, and head of the Shia in Baghdad.)

key_terms.زَاهِدٌ: ascetic, one who renounces worldly pleasures

ai.seo_question: What did the Ottoman encyclopedist Shams al-Din Sami write about Sheikh al-Mufid in Kamus al-A'lam?
ai.summary: This text quotes Shams al-Din Sami's Turkish encyclopedia 'Kamus al-A'lam' (p. 668) in praise of Sheikh al-Mufid (Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Baghdadi), describing him as one of the most celebrated scholars whose honorific title is al-Mufid. It highlights his high standing among the Buyid dynasty — to the extent that the Buyid ruler 'Adud al-Dawla visited him personally in his home — his prolific authorship, his asceticism and devotion, and his role as head of the Shia community in Baghdad.
